main_text.head: Quæ tãta[?], admiratione homines in se convertunt.
main_text.p: Ut est inter pisces balæna, inter quadrupedes unicornis, inter aves Monocodiata, aut qui à Tacito hic recenfetur Phœnix. Neque enim dentur ejufmodi animalia nécne, curatius explorare, politicæ difciplinæ est. Cornelii nos duētum fecuti, avem hanc, raritate aut fabulæ audacia infignem, articulatè contempla-bimur.Phœnicis contemplatio.

1. A Loco Ægypto. Post longum seculorum am-bitum avis Phœnix in Ægyptum venit. Ægyptus.Ægyptus est, quæ ut ingenia hominum varia ac mobilia, ita partus animalium portentosos gignit aut recipit. Hæc crocodilos, hæc hippopodamos, aquæ & terræ commora-tione ambiguos, hæc alia animantia, de quibus ad fa-stidium Diodorus Siculus; hæc cœli, terræ, aquarum miracula producit. Cœlum Ægypti ne in tenuem quidem pluviam, psecada[?] Græci appellant, nedum in largiorem imbrem, nisi prodigio, resolvitur. quod ac-cidisse prodigium, post debellatam cum Antonio Cleopatram, terra sub Romanorum jugum itura, Dio & ex eo Xiphilinus autores funt aquâ fluminis annuo incremento terram oppressam irrigans, excipiendo frugum fœtui mollit. Sic ut Nilo exundante, & rur-sum se intra ripas colligente, nix ulla terra Ægypto ubertate contendat. hæc eadem Ægyptus phœnicem,

page.notes: Running head and page number read from the scan. Doubtful readings: "tãta" in the chapter title (tilde reading uncertain); "psecada" (printed "pfecada", possibly a Greek word printed in Latin letters, copied as printed); "Cleopatram" and "fa-stidium" line-end readings; the running head's final letters. Long s printed as f has been normalised to s throughout ("eft" as est, "fi" as si in the catchword). Italic passage "oblitus Arruntium ... attineri" taken from the scan's italic type. Printing error left as printed: "nóftro" with stray accent (read as nostro). Greek word "psecada" not confirmed in Greek letters. The "1. A Loco Ægypto." run-in heading is treated as paragraph text, since it opens with a number.
